title: reading a repository
goal: A2 Answer “what changed, when, and by whom” without opening a browser
startWith: Clone something real and large enough to have history worth reading.

newIdeas.plain: The commit you are standing on. Almost every command is relative to it.
A name pointing at a commit: a branch, a tag, HEAD, origin/main.
A..B means “commits in B that are not in A”.

tasks.do: Clone a repository and read its shape

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git clone https://github.com/junit-team/junit5.git
cd junit5
git log --oneline -20
git log --graph --oneline --decorate -20

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: File → New → Project from Version Control. Same clone, and it opens the project afterwards.

tasks.do: Diff the three pairs that matter: working tree, index, and a commit
tasks.why: git diff with no arguments does not show staged changes. That surprise costs people a commit.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git diff                # working tree vs index
git diff --staged       # index vs HEAD: what a commit would contain
git diff HEAD~5 HEAD    # between two commits

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: Ctrl+D on two selected files, or select two commits in the Log and right-click → Compare Versions.

tasks.do: Filter history by file, author, message and date
tasks.why: “When did this get like that” is a search, and git indexes its own history.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git log --oneline -- README.md
git log --author="@" --since="3 months ago" --oneline
git log --grep="fix" --oneline -10
git log -p -1 -- README.md

check.expect: up to five commits touching this folder

tasks.do: Blame a file and jump from a line to the commit that wrote it
tasks.why: Blame answers “why is this here” faster than any comment.

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: Right-click the editor gutter → Annotate with Git Blame. Click an annotation to open the commit, hover for the message. The single most useful git feature in the IDE.

tasks.do: Search history for a string that no longer exists
tasks.why: -S (the “pickaxe”) finds the commit that added or removed a piece of text — how you find deleted code.

proof.note: You found who last changed a specific file, and why.

doneWhen: Given a line of code, you can name its commit, author and message in under a minute.

lessons.title: Annotate — blame in the gutter
lessons.teach: Right-click the editor gutter → Annotate with Git Blame. Each line gets its commit; click one to open it, hover for the message. This is git blame without leaving the line you were reading.

lessons.title: History for one file
lessons.teach: Right-click a file → Git → Show History. Every commit that touched it, with the diff for each — git log -p -- <file>, browsable.
